bib.title: Magicoder: Empowering Code Generation with OSS-INSTRUCT
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235, 2024

read.skipped: Appendix D/E generated-code examples skimmed only

question: Can instruction data generated by an LLM from random open-source code snippets give more diverse, less biased code instruction tuning than Self-Instruct or Evol-Instruct?
hypothesis: Seeding a teacher LLM with real open-source snippets mitigates the inherent bias of LLM-generated data and yields more diverse, realistic, controllable instruction data.
contributions: OSS-INSTRUCT, generating coding instruction data from open-source code snippets
Magicoder series (OSS-Instruct) and MagicoderS series (OSS-Instruct + Evol-Instruct), evaluated across 6 benchmarks
Open-sourced weights, training data and code

method.summary: A teacher (gpt-3.5-turbo-1106) is shown a random 1-15 line snippet from starcoderdata and writes a self-contained problem plus solution; about 75K cleaned pairs finetune CodeLlama-Python-7B or DeepSeek-Coder-Base-6.7B (Magicoder), then a further finetune on evol-codealpaca-v1 gives MagicoderS.
method.task: code instruction tuning with synthetic data (supervised finetuning)

datasets.name: OSS-Instruct
datasets.source: gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 outputs from seeds in starcoderdata (80K docs: 40K Python, 5K each of C++, Java, TypeScript, Shell, C#, Rust, PHP, Swift)
datasets.preprocessing: Dedup identical samples and samples sharing a seed; decontaminated vs HumanEval, MBPP, APPS docstrings, DS-1000, GSM8K (9 removed); noisy samples kept

datasets.name: evol-codealpaca-v1
datasets.source: theblackcat102 open reproduction of Evol-Instruct, generated by GPT-4

datasets.source: Chen et al. 2021; Liu et al. 2023b

parameters.data_generation_decoding: greedy decoding with gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 to maximise consistency of problem and solution

metrics.name: pass@1
metrics.definition: fraction of tasks whose generated code passes all tests

eval.protocol: Table 1 and 4 baselines taken from EvalPlus leaderboard (hash 1895d2f); MultiPL-E 7B models run with bigcode-evaluation-harness, others from WizardCoder paper; single run, no seeds or significance tests

prompts.text:
You are exceptionally skilled at crafting high-quality programming problems and offering precise solutions.
Please gain inspiration from the following random code snippet to create a high-quality programming problem. Present your output in two distinct sections: [Problem Description] and [Solution].
Code snippet for inspiration:
```
{code}
```
Guidelines for each section:
1. [Problem Description]: This should be **completely self-contained**, providing all the contextual information one needs to understand and solve the problem. Assume common programming knowledge, but ensure that any specific context, variables, or code snippets pertinent to this problem are explicitly included.
2. [Solution]: Offer a comprehensive, **correct** solution that accurately addresses the [Problem Description] you provided.

limits: Only models up to 7B parameters tested due to resource constraints (Appendix F).
The OSS-Instruct prompt is sophisticated and may need a strong teacher; weaker models may produce implausible data.
Single run, greedy decoding for main tables, no seeds or confidence intervals.
Baselines taken from EvalPlus leaderboard and the WizardCoder paper, not rerun; WizardCoder-CL-7B omitted from MultiPL-E for latency.
DeepSeek-Coder comparison is brief because its data and instruction tuning are undisclosed; token counts differ (+90M/+240M vs +2B).
Teacher is gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 for most data; distillation from the teacher is not fully separated except by the Mixtral 20K experiment.
Training objective details (loss masking, chat template) not stated.
